headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress can leak business data, while the pair otherwise shows no direct injection or write-conflict pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between airbyte and awesome-production-machine-learning, and neither profile shows a default path for one to ingest the other’s outputs. Airbyte exposes only the Airbyte API and broad egress; the awesome-list has no I/O surfaces. The interaction pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess prompt-injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw output as instructions, risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Disable any future file-based handoff between them.
Add provenance tags to any exchanged artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation for machine-readable outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive workspace contents if configured to do so. The awesome-production-machine-learning profile shows no data classes touched and no egress, so it is not itself a leak source. The pair risk is driven by Airbyte’s default-capable outbound path, with no compensating isolation documented.
conditions: IF Airbyte is connected to sources containing sensitive business data, leakage risk is present.
IF the pair shares a workspace or exported artifacts, Airbyte can exfiltrate those contents over network egress.
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte connectors to non-sensitive sources.
Place Airbyte in a network egress allowlist.
Separate workspaces so the awesome-list cannot stage files for Airbyte.
Review connector configs for secret-bearing fields.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress proxy controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. Airbyte only shows API access and broad network egress, while awesome-production-machine-learning has no I/O surfaces or write permissions. Without a shared mutable target, there is no plausible capability conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or database, reassess conflict risk.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources single-writer.
Avoid mounting the same directory into both agents.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce pipeline outputs, but the awesome-production-machine-learning profile is an awesome-list with no runnable actions or downstream authority. That makes a harmful cascade unlikely: there is no documented path where B blindly acts on A’s output. Uncertainty is low because B lacks execution surfaces.
conditions: IF B is repurposed to auto-ingest Airbyte outputs into an action-taking workflow, cascade risk increases.
IF A’s outputs are treated as authoritative without validation, reassess.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action.
Require schema validation on Airbyte outputs.
Keep B read-only and non-executing.
Log and diff all imported records.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and may move it across systems, while awesome-production-machine-learning touches no data classes and has no residency or retention controls documented. The only concrete compliance concern is Airbyte’s handling of business data; the second profile does not add a documented mismatch, so the pairwise issue is limited.
conditions: IF Airbyte processes regulated business data under a stricter residency or retention policy, compliance review is needed.
IF the pair is used to store or redistribute governed data, reassess policy alignment.
mitigations: Classify the business data before ingestion.
Limit Airbyte to approved regions.
Document retention settings for any synced datasets.
Keep the awesome-list free of governed data.
requires-engineering: implement policy checks on data movement.
